chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you desire a need, pray two Rak'at, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and ask, and you will be given it.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer and supplication method for fulfilling a specific need in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes the *Salāt al-Hājah* as a fundamental devotional practice in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the intercessory role of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt. The promise of acceptance ('you will be given') underscores the spiritual efficacy of combining ritual prayer with specific blessings, reflecting the Shia belief in the closeness of the Imams to divine will.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Al-Haris Bin Al-Mugheira,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whenever you want a need, so pray two Rak’at of Salāt, and send Blessings upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and ask, you would be Given it’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from al-Flarith ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you need something, perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer) and say, “Allahumma Salli ‘Ala Muhammad wa ‘Ali Muhammad (O Allah grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause).” Ask for your needs. They will be fulfilled.’”
